title: Microsoft Teams Service Disruption Hits Meetings and Screen Sharing
content_md: Microsoft confirmed early Wednesday that a service disruption prevented some customers from using multiple Microsoft Teams features , including meeting creation, joining meetings, and screen sharing. In an update posted at 7:26 a.m. IST on August 26, 2026, the company said that monitoring indicated the issue had largely been mitigated. Engineers would continue observing the platform for 15 to 30 minutes to verify that the fault did not recur. The outage appears to have hit Teams meetings first. Users reported trouble joining or creating meetings, while some attendees who entered calls could not share their screens. Microsoft Teams Service Disruption ITmedia said Japanese users began posting after 9:00 a.m. local time that meeting access had failed; “Teams” then trended on X. Several users said one-to-one calls remained available, suggesting a problem concentrated in meeting services rather than a complete Teams client failure. For security and IT operations teams, that split is consequential. Failed meeting joins, creation workflows, and in-meeting collaboration can interrupt incident bridges, SOC huddles, executive escalations, and tabletop exercises. Organizations that rely on Teams as their primary emergency channel should classify a broad collaboration failure as a continuity event rather than merely a productivity issue.
